rule_metadata.description: Comprehensive rules governing the semi-vowel soft lengthening of Waw or Ya Saakinah preceded by a Fathah when pausing (Waqf) on a word.

theoretical_foundation.linguistic_definition: Layyin (لَيِّن) literally means softness, ease, or smoothness in Arabic.
theoretical_foundation.applied_tajweed_definition: Madd al-Layyin occurs when a Waw Saakinah (وْ) or Ya Saakinah (يْ) is preceded specifically by a Fathah letter, and the reciter pauses (Waqf) on the subsequent letter, creating a temporary Sukoon.
theoretical_foundation.ruling_and_duration: A permissible elongation of **2, 4, or 6 counts** (Harakat) upon stopping, exactly matching the mechanics of Madd 'Arid lis-Sukoon.
theoretical_foundation.wasl_ruling: If the reciter continues reading without stopping (Wasl), the Layyin letters are pronounced smoothly with zero elongation (normal short count).
theoretical_foundation.mushaf_indicator: A Fathah on the letter preceding a vowelless Waw or Ya, combined with pausing at the end of the word.

practical_examples.breakdown: Ya Saakinah preceded by Ra with Fathah; when pausing on Quraysh, elongated 2, 4, or 6 counts.
Waw Saakinah preceded by Kha with Fathah; soft lengthening applied upon pausing.
Ya Saakinah preceded by Sad with Fathah.

assessment_bank.question: What does 'Layyin' mean linguistically?
What letters form the foundation of Madd al-Layyin?
options: Waw Saakinah or Ya Saakinah preceded by a Fathah

assessment_bank.question: What vowel must precede the Waw or Ya for Madd al-Layyin to apply?
What is the permissible duration range for Madd al-Layyin when pausing?
What action triggers Madd al-Layyin to become active?
options: Pausing (Waqf) on the word, creating a temporary Sukoon on the final letter

assessment_bank.question: What happens to Madd al-Layyin if you continue reading without stopping (Wasl)?
options: The lengthening disappears and it is read as a smooth, short semi-vowel with zero elongation

assessment_bank.question: In the word 'قُرَيْشٍ', when stopping at the end of the ayah, what rule applies?
In the phrase 'مِنْ خَوْفٍ', when pausing on 'خَوْفٍ', what Tajweed rule governs the Waw?
options: Madd al-Layyin (Waw Saakinah preceded by Fathah)

assessment_bank.question: How does Madd al-Layyin differ from standard Madd Tabii or 'Arid?
options: Layyin specifically uses semi-vowels Waw/Ya preceded by Fathah rather than matching Dammah/Kasrah homing vowels

assessment_bank.question: In 'وَالصَّيْفِ', stopping on it invokes which rule?
What is the phonetic character of Layyin letters compared to strict Madd letters?
options: They are pronounced with extreme smoothness and ease off the tongue

assessment_bank.question: If a student chooses a 4-count length for Madd al-Layyin in Surah Quraysh, should they maintain it?
options: Yes, consistency in rhythm throughout the reading session is standard practice
No, it must change every word

Which of the following words features a Ya Layyin?
What similarity does Madd al-Layyin share with Madd 'Arid lis-Sukoon?
options: Both activate upon pausing and share the identical permissible count options (2, 4, or 6 counts)

assessment_bank.question: If a reciter connects 'قُرَيْشٍ' directly to the next word without pausing, how is the Ya treated?
options: Read smoothly with normal short vowel tempo and zero soft elongation

assessment_bank.question: In Surah Quraysh, how many opportunities for Madd al-Layyin appear?
options: Multiple (e.g., إِيلَافِهِمْ رِحْلَةَ الشِّتَاءِ وَالصَّيْفِ and قُرَيْشٍ)

assessment_bank.question: What error does an AI evaluation engine flag if a student adds a 6-count Layyin lengthening while connecting words in Wasl?
options: Inappropriate elongation of Layyin letter during continuous unpaused recitation

assessment_bank.question: Why are Waw and Ya in Layyin called semi-vowels?
options: Because they retain a glide quality while being vowelless, preceded by an open Fathah

assessment_bank.question: In 'عَلَيْف' or similar contexts, what governs the Ya?
What is the exact counting pulse required for a 4-count Madd al-Layyin pause?
options: A steady 4-beat rhythm maintaining vocal resonance

assessment_bank.question: Can Madd al-Layyin occur in the middle of an uninterrupted verse sentence?
options: No, the lengthening component strictly requires a pause (Waqf) or temporary Sukoon trigger

assessment_bank.question: In 'فَلْيَعْبُدُوا رَبَّ هَذَا الْبَيْتِ', when stopping on 'الْبَيْتِ', what rule applies?
How does the mouth shape differ between Waw Layyin and Ya Layyin?
options: Waw Layyin rounds the lips; Ya Layyin flattens the tongue and lowers the jaw slightly

assessment_bank.question: What is the relationship between Madd al-Layyin and Aqwa al-Mudud hierarchy?
options: It ranks similarly to Madd 'Arid lis-Sukoon since both depend on temporary pausing sukoon

assessment_bank.question: In 'الَّذِي أَطْعَمَهُمْ مِنْ جُوعٍ وَآمَنَهُمْ مِنْ خَوْفٍ', stopping on 'خَوْفٍ' triggers what rule?
What is the visual clue in the Arabic script for recognizing a potential Layyin opportunity?
options: A Fathah on a consonant directly preceding a vowelless Waw or Ya at a pause point

assessment_bank.question: If a student recites Madd al-Layyin with 2 counts, is it valid?
options: Yes, 2, 4, or 6 counts are all fully permissible upon stopping

assessment_bank.question: What is the pedagogical goal of including Madd al-Layyin in your elite Tajweed app?
options: To ensure comprehensive coverage of semi-vowel pause mechanics across all Quranic styles

assessment_bank.question: Summarize the complete mechanism of Madd al-Layyin:
options: Encounter Waw/Ya Saakinah preceded by Fathah -> pause on the word (Waqf) -> apply permissible 2, 4, or 6 count soft elongation -> drop elongation if connecting in Wasl

assessment_bank.question: In 'بَيْنِ', when pausing, what rule applies?
In 'شَيْءٍ', when pausing on it, does Layyin apply?
options: Yes, Ya Saakinah preceded by Fathah on Sheen

assessment_bank.question: How does pausing on 'شَيْءٍ' affect the Hamzah and Ya?
options: Creates a soft Layyin glide on the Ya when stopping

assessment_bank.question: What is the primary acoustic distinction between a natural vowel Madd and a Layyin semi-vowel Madd?
options: Layyin glides from an open Fathah mouth posture into a semi-vowel, whereas Tabii follows a matching homing vowel

assessment_bank.question: If a reciter uses 6 counts for Layyin in Surah Quraysh, is it accepted in authentic Tajweed transmission?
options: Yes, 6 counts is one of the three valid permissible options (2, 4, 6)

assessment_bank.question: What happens to the rhythm of recitation when mastering Madd al-Layyin?
options: It adds exquisite smoothness and melodic cadence to verse-ending pauses

assessment_bank.question: Which Quranic Surah is famously taught first when introducing Madd al-Layyin to students?
options: Surah Quraysh (due to قُرَيْشٍ and الصَّيْفِ)

assessment_bank.question: Can Madd al-Layyin be combined with other stopping rules like Hams or Qalqalah?
options: Yes, when stopping on words ending in other letters preceded by a Layyin semi-vowel

assessment_bank.question: How should an AI evaluation engine score a student who pauses on 'قُرَيْشٍ' with a steady 4-count soft glide?
options: Mark as correct and fully compliant with valid Layyin pause options

assessment_bank.question: Summarize the core rule of Madd al-Layyin in one definitive statement:
options: Waw or Ya Saakinah preceded by Fathah allows a permissible 2, 4, or 6 count soft elongation only when pausing on the word
